Add mark command for completed tasks
Add Task class for task state

commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot classes are in the default package and keep some style-sensitive values as local variables.

The SE-EDU Java standard expects classes to be placed in packages and constants to follow conventional naming.

Let's move the chatbot classes into the wenwen package, tighten task field visibility, extract constants, and update the README path to the packaged main class.

The project needs a reusable way to inspect code changes across multiple files.

A project-local skill keeps that workflow available without rediscovering the generator command each time.

Let's add the present-changes-visually skill and its split-view HTML diff generator.

Java style expectations come from the SE-EDU coding standard and should be easy to apply consistently.

A project-local skill captures the relevant conventions for Java edits in this repository.

Let's add a seedu-java-coding-standard skill with routing metadata and the key project rules.

Commit and branch naming rules should be applied consistently across future project work.

A project-local skill makes the SE-EDU Git conventions available when proposing or creating commits.

Let's add a seedu-git-standard skill with routing metadata and the key message rules.

The repository now has project-local skills for SE-EDU Java and Git conventions.

Agent instructions should point future work to those skills so the standards are applied consistently.

Let's update AGENTS.md to require the Java standard for code edits and the Git standard for commit and branch guidance.

Support todo, deadline, and event commands using Task subclasses so each task type owns its display format. This completes the Level-4 behavior while applying the inheritance extension expected for this increment.

Refactor Wenwen command handling into smaller helper methods to reduce the size and complexity of main. This keeps command parsing, task updates, and output formatting easier to read and maintain for the next increments.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task deletion with a dynamic list
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the fixed-size task array with an ArrayList so deletion renumbers remaining entries naturally and removes the arbitrary capacity limit.

Validate delete commands using the same index handling as mark and unmark.

Load tasks from an OS-independent relative data path at startup and save changes through an atomic file replacement.

Encode user-entered fields safely, create missing folders automatically, and recover gracefully when saved data is missing, unreadable, or corrupted.

Set the application entry point and Shadow output name so the generated artifact runs directly with java -jar.

Use a provisioned Java 25 toolchain and document how to build, locate, and run the distributable JAR.

Wenwen currently owns user interaction, parsing, task operations, and
application control in one class, which makes each responsibility harder to
extend and test independently.

Extract Ui, Parser, and TaskList components and represent each user action as
a Command. Keep Wenwen focused on application setup and orchestration, and add
regression tests for parsing, task operations, persistence, and a full session.

Deadline and event timing is currently stored as unstructured text, so invalid
values cannot be rejected and dated tasks cannot be queried reliably.

Store deadlines as LocalDate and events as LocalDateTime, use strict portable
input formats and friendly display formats, and add an on-date query for dated
tasks. Cover parsing, formatting, date matching, and persistence with tests.

Users cannot currently locate tasks without scanning the full list.

Add a find command that performs a case-insensitive substring search over task
descriptions and presents matches in their original order. Reject empty search
terms and add parser, task-list, and end-to-end regression coverage.

The public API is documented, but several parsing and orchestration helpers
still require readers to infer their contracts, and implicit command
constructors produce JavaDoc warnings.

Document the remaining non-trivial private methods and add explicit documented
constructors so generated JavaDoc describes the complete design without
warnings.

The published documentation is still a placeholder and does not explain how
to start Wenwen or use its commands.

Replace it with a concise user-focused guide covering setup, every feature,
date and time formats, automatic persistence, example responses, error
recovery, and a command reference.
